record: The frozen production schema the forward-migration checks are run against. Captured read-only on 2026-11-10 by the capture-production-baseline workflow (pg_dump 17.11; run 42735887806, artifact production-baseline-7; the pg_dump path and fingerprint fixes are PR #19 and PR #20). It is a full logical dump (COPY-format data) and DOES contain real rows, so it lives only in gitignored backups/; the verification tool loads its schema and skips every data statement. A read-only data fingerprint of the same capture sits alongside the artifact (backups/fingerprint-production-2026-11-10T01-29-04.json, 32 protected tables, 105 rows). Production is never a migrate target: it is checked against, never written.
dataNote: Measured with the project splitter: 1143 statements total, 92 of them data (COPY rows, all skipped, never executed). The loader also skips 42 scaffold/extension/stub statements (3 scaffold-schema, 4 extension-unavailable, 4 scaffold-function, 30 stub-table, 1 scaffold-publication) — see scripts/lib/baseline.mjs. Contains personal data and password hashes — never commit, never publish. The tool re-measures this count and refuses the record if it does not match.

ledgerOnServer.note: The server's own supabase_migrations bookkeeping at capture time: versions 0009-0016, 0179, 0181, 0190, 0199-0232, 0290, 0303, 0304. It does not match the repository directory (296 files, newest 0304); that divergence is exactly why this baseline exists and why history is never replayed.

policy.note: No migration file from supabase/migrations may be replayed onto production as history. Production moves only by individually verified NEW files (0303+), at the release gate, through the sanctioned path.
